chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who raised it (to the Imam), saying:
A time will come upon people when well-being will consist of ten parts: nine of them are keeping away from people, and one is silence.

key_terms.اعْتِزَالُ النَّاسِ: Keeping away from people / social withdrawal
key_terms.الْعَافِيَة: Well-being, safety, or deliverance from trials

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of silence and social withdrawal in Shia ethics according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a diagnostic of the 'era of concealment' (Zaman al-Kufr), where social interaction often leads to spiritual compromise, making withdrawal (i'tizal) a primary mechanism for preserving faith. This interpretation aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not merely as physical poverty, but as a strategic disengagement from corrupt societal norms to maintain inner purity. The attribution of nine-tenths of well-being to this withdrawal underscores the severity of the trials faced by the faithful in mixed company.
